full_judgment:
9. Section 34 of the Ordinance provides, Infer alia, that a worker can enforce any right secured by or under any law and prescribes no period of limitation. 

 10. As regards the third point Mr. Shafique Ahmed has reformulated it in a different way before us. He contends that the benefit under section 34 of the Ordinance extending to an individual worker was extended to him, if at all, when the Industrial Relations Ordinance, 1969 was amended on the 17th October, 1970, and on that date his right of termination benefit under section 19 of the Standing Orders Act had become barred, and so the right itself was extinguished. There was, therefore, no such right secured under the law available to the worker for enforcement when the said section came into existence and when the application was filed on 9.11.70. This argument though ingenious, yet it does not stand the scruting of reasoning. Firstly, we are applying provisions of Section 34 of the Industrial Relations Ordinance which is a different enactment and there is no such bar of limitation therein as has been contended. Secondly, the argument is fallacious in view of the fact that under the provisions of the Standing Orders Act what was barred was the remedy under it, but the right secured to a worker under section 19 were not extinguished. There is a great distinction between the barring of a remedy and extinguishment of a right. Nothing could be found in Standing Orders Act to read that after the prescribed period under Section 25 the right secured under the Act will also be extinguished. There being no such express bar, the ordinary principle of the interpretation of Statutes will apply. The rule is that limitation restricts rights to take legal action for enforcement of a existing right after the lapse of certain period. It does not extinguish the right but simply bars the enforcement of the said right after certain lapse of time. We find that the right survived and the Ordinance secured to the worker that right and also gave him remedy for its enforcement without prescribing any period of limitation. The point advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner fails.
